title.title: A split tangent bundle makes the universal cover a product
title.subtitle: Claim: if $T_X = E_1 \oplus E_2$ with both summands integrable, the universal cover of $X$ is a product

plain: If every direction splits cleanly into two kinds, the whole space unrolls into a product, like a grid

panels.caption: rows: leaves of $E_1$, columns: leaves of $E_2$ (schematic)

beats.text: Locally, two foliations give product charts: Frobenius
The hard part is continuing the charts globally, box by box
Claimed: globally, the universal cover splits as a product

steps: Locally, the two foliations give product boxes
Grow the boxes, extending across their edges (Hartogs)
The boxes stitch into one global product

achievement.label: Beauville's splitting conjecture (2000), two summands
statement: T_X = E_1 \oplus E_2 \;\Rightarrow\; \tilde X \cong X_1 \times X_2
achievement.context: Before: surfaces, threefolds and special classes (Brunella–Pereira–Touzet, Höring)
achievement.note: Two integrable summands only; Beauville allows any number

verify.detail: Formalized on custom complex-manifold foundations, worth an audit
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean scope notes; we did not build the Lean

voice.text: If the tangent bundle splits in two integrable pieces, the cover should be a product.
Grow product boxes and extend them across their edges, until they cover everything.
Claimed: the two-summand case of Beauville.

sources.quote: Beauville ('Complex manifolds with split tangent bundle', 2000) conjectured universal-cover splitting
Beauville's full conjecture allows any number of summands and does not assume integrability
It is formalized (`OAI/Geometry/KahlerSplitting/Main.lean:14`), on custom complex-manifold foundations.
